answer: Adaptive Arrival-Spacing Gate assigns each new identity a required minimum inter-arrival gap drawn from a slowly updated fable of normal cadence, so bursts compress admissible throughput rather than raising it. A raven-like scout that opens many identities in parallel finds each subsequent admission delayed geometrically, forcing serialized waiting. The resulting ripple in onboarding timing reveals coordination without inspecting content. Cost: an attacker must occupy real wall-clock time per identity, so N identities cost roughly N²/2 wait-units, making mass registration impractical.
